name: file.rename
description: Move or rename a file. Files only — use `directory.rename` for directories. The destination's parent directory determines whether it's a rename (same parent) or a move (different parent).

dst.description: New absolute path. Parent directory must exist.

overwrite.description: If true, replace `dst` if it exists. Without this flag, an existing `dst` returns ERR already_exists.

cross_fs.description: If true, allow a copy+delete fallback when `src` and `dst` are on different filesystems. Without this flag, cross-filesystem moves return ERR cross_device. The fallback is non-atomic (a concurrent reader may see partial state).

fallback_used.description: `copy_delete` when the cross-filesystem fallback was engaged (only possible with `cross_fs: true`); `none` otherwise.

x-implementations.name: move_file_ex
x-implementations.description: Win32 `MoveFileExW(src, dst, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING? | MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED?)`. Atomic when src and dst are on the same filesystem; copies + deletes when MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED is set and they're on different volumes.

x-implementations.name: copy_delete_fallback
x-implementations.description: 9x non-atomic fallback when MoveFileEx is unavailable: CopyFile + DeleteFile. For directory rename on 9x: CreateDirectory + recursive copy + RemoveDirectory.

windows-modern.description: MoveFileExW. Atomic same-volume rename; cross-volume requires `cross_fs: true` to engage MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED. Returns ERR already_exists when dst exists and overwrite is false. Long paths via `\\?\` prefix automatic.

windows-classic.description: MoveFileEx on NT 4+; CopyFile+DeleteFile fallback on 9x. Same-volume renames are atomic on NT; 9x is never atomic. Cross-volume always copy+delete; `cross_fs: true` is the explicit opt-in.
